name: Ink
backing: Individuals: Vadim Demedes (creator) and Sindre Sorhus (most active maintainer recently). No company.

notable_users: Claude Code (originally; now React on Anthropic's own renderer)
adoption.summary: The default terminal renderer for the JS agent wave; README lists Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Copilot CLI first.

maintainability.bus_factor: medium: two well-known maintainers, no company; very wide downstream use
maintainability.summary: Revived and moving fast in 2026 (v7 overhauled input, v8 requires React 19.3+, adds scroll offsets and finer incremental rendering).

architecture.summary: A custom React reconciler builds a tree of Box/Text host nodes laid out with Yoga (flexbox); on each commit Ink renders the tree to a string and writes it to stdout, either redrawing the dynamic region or, with incrementalRendering, only changed lines (v8 skips unchanged line prefixes). <Static> writes permanent output above the live region, which is what lets CLIs keep native scrollback. Hooks (useInput, usePaste, useFocus, useBoxMetrics, useWindowSize) give input and measurement; options cover alternateScreen, maxFps (default 30), concurrent React, kitty keyboard, screen-reader output.
key_points: Full React: components, hooks, context, Suspense, concurrent mode
React DevTools integration: inspect and edit props live in a running CLI
ink-testing-library: render() returns lastFrame(), frames[], stdin.write()

claims.text: maxFps default 30; incrementalRendering 'can reduce flickering and improve performance'

Claude Code left Ink's renderer: '<Static> creates a hard boundary… updates were suppressed or triggered full redraws'; Anthropic's React-based rewrite (cell diffing, double buffering, damage tracking, DEC 2026) cut offscreen flicker ~85%
Claude Code later added a fullscreen NO_FLICKER renderer that virtualizes the viewport; default for users first seen on/after 2026-05-06

performance.summary: Ink publishes no benchmarks; the best public evidence is negative (Claude Code's rewrite) plus upstream fixes (incremental rendering, PR #781; v8 prefix skipping).

agent_usability.how: Code generation (agents write Ink/React fluently). Live: React DevTools over its WebSocket backend can inspect the tree and edit props of a running CLI (DEV=true). Declarative-UI projects use Ink as the terminal target: A2UI (a2ui-ink) and json-render (@json-render/ink) map JSON specs onto Ink components.
agent_usability.integration_effort: Low for code-gen; for live control you either speak the React DevTools protocol or put a JSON spec layer (A2UI/json-render) in front of Ink.
agent_usability.readback: React DevTools shows the component tree and props; ink-testing-library gives lastFrame() text in tests; otherwise screen scraping.
agent_usability.granular_edits: DevTools prop edits (human-oriented); via json-render/A2UI, spec-level patches.
agent_usability.summary: Not agent-drivable by itself, but the de facto terminal backend that JSON agent-UI specs compile to.

score_notes.ui_as_data: JSX; A2UI/json-render add a JSON layer on top, but that is not Ink
score_notes.agent_drivable: React DevTools live prop editing is an API, but human-oriented; no agent protocol
score_notes.readback: Structured tree via DevTools; lastFrame() in tests
score_notes.live_data_rate: 30 fps default cap; no throughput numbers
score_notes.pixel_graphics: No image support in core found

steelman: Ink made the terminal a React target, and that single idea is why the agent CLI wave happened in JavaScript: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Wrangler, Shopify and Prisma all shipped on it, and 7.8M installs a week follow. Every frontend engineer — and every model — already knows how to write it; components, hooks, context and Suspense just work, with Yoga flexbox for layout. Its default inline mode with <Static> output keeps native scrollback, selection and Cmd+F, a trade-off Anthropic explicitly defended for Claude Code. Ink is also where declarative agent UI lands in the terminal today: A2UI's official terminal renderer and json-render both target Ink, so a JSON spec from an agent becomes a live Ink tree with no new runtime. React DevTools lets you inspect and edit a running CLI's props live. In 2026 it is actively maintained again, with incremental rendering, kitty keyboard, scroll views and screen-reader support.
weaknesses: Line-oriented string rendering: Anthropic left it for a cell-diffing renderer because <Static> 'fights React's model' and caused full redraws
No agent protocol or structured readback outside DevTools/tests
Maintained by individuals; breaking majors in 2026 (v7, v8)

relation_to_scene.overlap: Declarative component tree, keyed reconciliation preserving view state (scene's ids work like React keys), terminal renderer for JSON agent-UI specs (via A2UI/json-render).
relation_to_scene.scene_reinvents: Reconciliation keyed by id and a component vocabulary; for JS hosts, A2UI+Ink already gives 'agent sends JSON, terminal renders it'.
borrow: <Static>/inline mode: an optional non-fullscreen scene mode that keeps native scrollback
ink-testing-library's lastFrame()/frames[] as the shape of scene's screen readback
React DevTools' live prop editing as a model for patch-by-id UX
Interop: accept the same JSON A2UI/json-render emit to Ink
relation_to_scene.gap_left: Cell-level diffing renderer, socket control of a live instance, readback of state + screen, data streams that bypass the model, pixel layer, hot-swap, time travel.
relation_to_scene.verdict_why: Ink is the terminal target of the JS/A2UI world; scene should interoperate with the specs that target Ink rather than compete with Ink itself.
